mission: Establish the first local psychological foundations corpus for the Teacher Mind so tutoring rests on serious learning science before specialization into support profiles or impairment-aware adaptations.
collection_principles: Prefer consensus reports, institutional syntheses, and highly cited review articles before collecting many narrow studies.
Translate psychology into bounded teaching implications rather than diagnosis claims.
Favor sources that can directly change tutoring decisions about pacing, chunking, retrieval, feedback, and learner confidence.
Include anti-myth guardrails so the Teacher Mind does not absorb popular but weakly supported educational beliefs.
core_questions: How do encoding, retrieval, spacing, and retention affect durable learning?
Why do some learning strategies feel effective while producing weak long-term retention?
How should a tutor reason about cognitive load, working-memory pressure, and explanation chunking?
How should a tutor treat learner confidence, motivation, and self-efficacy without becoming therapeutic?
Which widespread educational myths should be excluded from the Teacher Mind policy layer?

domains.name: Learning and Memory
domains.goal: Ground explanation and review in encoding, retention, forgetting, and durable learning.

domains.name: Retrieval and Spacing
domains.goal: Support practice strategies that privilege recall and delayed retention over short-term fluency.

domains.name: Cognitive Load and Working Limits
domains.goal: Guide step size, notation density, and pacing decisions.

domains.name: Motivation and Self-Efficacy
domains.goal: Help the tutor preserve agency and productive persistence without empty encouragement.

domains.name: Metacognition
domains.goal: Help the tutor distinguish confidence from understanding and design better checks for understanding.

domains.name: Anti-Myth Guardrails
domains.goal: Block unsupported teaching myths from becoming policy defaults.

starter_sources.title: How People Learn II: Learners, Contexts, and Cultures
starter_sources.organization: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
starter_sources.why_it_matters: High-credibility synthesis on learning, development, context, memory, attention, and implications for educational design.

starter_sources.title: How People Learn: Brain, Mind, Experience, and School
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Foundational earlier synthesis that strongly shaped modern conversations about prior knowledge, metacognition, transfer, and expert learning.

starter_sources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology
starter_sources.organization: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Often-cited synthesis comparing common study strategies and highlighting strong versus weak evidence for techniques such as practice testing and distributed practice.

starter_sources.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Classic demonstration that retrieval practice can improve delayed retention more than restudying.

starter_sources.title: The Critical Importance of Retrieval for Learning
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Important follow-up showing the special value of retrieval for durable learning and the gap between felt fluency and actual retention.

starter_sources.title: Organizing Instruction and Study to Improve Student Learning
starter_sources.organization: Institute of Education Sciences / What Works Clearinghouse
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Practical bridge from cognitive psychology to classroom moves, including spacing, quizzing, concrete-abstract links, and question design.

starter_sources.title: Using Student Achievement Data to Support Instructional Decision Making
starter_sources.organization: Institute of Education Sciences / What Works Clearinghouse
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Useful for formative decision-making, progress monitoring, and treating learner performance as feedback for instruction rather than fixed ability.

starter_sources.title: Learning Styles: Concepts and Evidence
starter_sources.organization: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Core guardrail source against turning learning-styles claims into Teacher Mind policy logic without evidence.
